subject: Availability elevation request from Synapse - proposed commitments
messages:
From: Samir Mehta <samir@synapse.io>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@synapse.io
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Elevated availability commitment for Synapse production

Hi Lauren / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Synapse is excited about the performance improvements on your new runtime. Leadership flagged an ask on our side: for our core transaction routing workload we'd like a written commitment to higher availability than your standard SLA while we go live (targeting an enterprise go-live in Q4).

Attached is a short form (Synapse_SLA_Request.pdf) that outlines the desired coverage window and uptime target. High level asks: 99.995% availability during 24x7 business hours for the first 12 months, multi-region failover within 3 minutes, and a financial credit schedule for outages above the threshold.

We know this is exceptional — happy to work with you on a realistic mutual action plan and any additional controls you require (dedicated capacity, ingress limits, runbook access). Can you confirm whether this is something Redwood can consider and what the expected cadence for an answer would be?

Regards,
Samir Mehta
Director of Infrastructure, Synapse Inc

Attachments:
- Synapse_SLA_Request.pdf (form)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Team — forwarding Synapse's request. Synapse is a strategic expansion opportunity; Aditya, you're shepherding the deal, but I want to make sure we surface the product and SRE constraints early. Quick asks:

- Marcus: what's feasible on the runtime side for a near-term 99.995% during business hours? What changes or guarantees would we need (dedicated pools, cross-region hot standby, additional monitoring hooks)?
- Grace: what does CS/ops need for runbook access and exec-run practices for a high-touch launch?
- Naomi: if we need to escalate commercially, do you anticipate leadership-level sign-off for an SLA amendment with credits?

Please respond with a realistic list of requirements and an estimated timeline for delivery. Synapse would like a written position this week if possible. I attached the Synapse form they provided.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Lauren / team — technical summary and proposed delivery options below. Short version: we can support an elevated commercial commitment with a combination of Dedicated capacity + multi-region hot standby + runbook/RBAC changes, but it requires a small set of short-term engineering work and an ops onboarding window. Details: 

Feasibility (near-term, 8-12 weeks):
- Availability target: 99.995% is achievable during a defined coverage window if Synapse is on Dedicated capacity with pinned model versions and region lock. Standard shared-hosted pools cannot meet that reliably for enterprise traffic.
- Failover: multi-region failover within 3 minutes requires warm standby with automated routing and KV cache priming. We have prototype support for cross-region replication but need to enable stable automated priming across the customer's working set (2-3 weeks engineering) and a runbook for manual intervention.
- Observability hooks: we'll provide token-level traces and per-route latency SLI dashboards; need to extend retention to 90 days as part of the agreement (work item).

Required changes (work items):
1) Provision dedicated GPU pool for Synapse (config + capacity planning) — infra ops (~1 week to provision once commit is signed).
2) Implement and test cross-region KV priming for active/passive failover (~2-3 weeks engineering + 1 week QA).
3) Update RBAC to provide Synapse read-only runbook traces and joint postmortem access (~1 week).
4) Draft runbook and SLO burn procedures with CS and SRE (~1 week).

Attachments I will add to the thread: proposed_sla_matrix.xlsx (draft SLA with measurable SLOs and credit table) and runbook_outline.md (high-level runbook checklist). These will include blackout windows and maintenance windows to protect the target.

Risk notes:
- If Synapse requires shared model variants or frequent model updates, the availability target becomes harder and we'd need stricter change windows.
- Cost: dedicated capacity + cross-region standby increases unit cost ~35-60% depending on load profile. We should present a delta with clear assumptions.

Happy to walk through this with Aditya and Synapse next week.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced:
- proposed_sla_matrix.xlsx
- runbook_outline.md
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Samir Mehta <samir@synapse.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Elevated availability commitment for Synapse production

Hi Samir — short note from our side with a proposed mutual action plan. First, thanks for the clarity in the form; gives us a good starting point. Per our internal review (Marcus + CS): we can consider the elevated commitment if Synapse agrees to the following path:

1) Contract amendment that specifies Dedicated capacity, the proposed SLO matrix (we'll share the draft), and a maintenance window schedule.
2) Procurement completes a standard security attestation and signs our amendment within 30 days of the mutual action plan.
3) Payment of the first two months' committed capacity as a deposit to cover upfront provisioning costs (we'll provide exact numbers once we size the pool).

Proposed timeline:
- This week: Redwood shares proposed_sla_matrix.xlsx and a redlined amendment template.
- Week 1-2: Synapse procurement review + security paperwork.
- Week 3-6: Provisioning and engineering work (cross-region priming + runbook prep).
- Week 7: Cutover and verification.

Commercial delta: rough estimate 40-55% uplift on standard Hosted pricing depending on peak TPS and token throughput. We can provide a precise quote if you share expected traffic profile (TPS, token/req).

I've CC'd Procurement (procurement@synapse.io) so they can confirm internal timelines. Happy to schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk through the proposed_sla_matrix and open items.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Internal approval request: elevated availability commitment for Synapse (decision required)

Naomi — I'm escalating to you for an approval decision and any leadership guidance. Synapse is asking for a 99.995% availability commitment with credits and 3-minute failover. Marcus and CS have outlined a feasible engineering path that requires Dedicated capacity + 3-6 weeks of prep work and a small commercial uplift (~40-55%).

We need a leadership sign-off on two things to proceed with the mutual action plan:
1) Approval to offer the SLA amendment with the attached SLO/credit table (proposed_sla_matrix.xlsx).
2) Approval to require a deposit (first two months' committed capacity) to cover provisioning risk.

If you approve, I will:
- Share the draft amendment with Synapse and Procurement this week.
- Kick off the capacity planning with infra and provide a sizing estimate within 48 hours.
- Schedule a joint kickoff call for next Tuesday.

If you think this requires an exec-level exception beyond what you can approve, please advise and I will route accordingly. We need an answer by EOD Monday to keep Synapse in our preferred window.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
